edits.old: | TC-E2-014-12 | Principle 5 | NFR | The decision log write forced to fail during an approval; the notice stays Generated |
edits.new:
| TC-E2-014-12 | Principle 5 | NFR | The decision log write forced to fail during an approval; the notice stays Generated |
| TC-E2-014-13 | BR9 | NFR | The approval, the inputs reference and the decision entry are written only to rwb_decision; no cross-schema read or join is made |
| TC-E2-014-14 | BR10 | NFR | The outcome leaves as one local decision record through the decision-record library on rwb.decision-record.v1 and no new event of this service is emitted |
| TC-E2-014-15 | BR11 | NFR | The age limits, override reasons, status values, product groups, role codes and template variants are read as parameters and reference data with the version in force |
| TC-E2-014-16 | BR12 | NFR | The screen is served through the gateway-bff composite route, and the route masks the identifiers, codes and dates the service returns |
| TC-E2-014-17 | BR13 | NFR | A cross-service call past its 2 s budget is answered as missing, never approves a notice and never shows a stale fact as current |
| TC-E2-014-18 | BR14 | NFR | The escalation of an unanswered D7.1 approval runs as a durable timer in ApprovalWorkflow and not as a scheduled job |
| TC-E2-014-19 | BR15 | NFR | A D7.1 notice carries no amount limit and the DoA table is not consulted for it |
| TC-E2-014-20 | BR16 | NFR | No event, log, workflow input or test carries a name, an address, an account number or a notice body |
